newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Micron busy on stock strength.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Micron busy on stock strength.

text.p: Options on Micron Technology Inc drew heavy interest Monday as the stock played catch-up to other technology stocks, rallying sharply.
In afternoon trading, Micron was up 2-1/8 at 47-1/4 on consolidated turnover of about 7.6 million shares.
It was below its intraday high of 47-11/16, a level not seen since December 1995 when the stock was dropping off its September 1995 peaks above 90.
"The stock's been a laggard" in the rallying technology group, one options trader in Chicago said. "It also looks good on some charts."
Rob Kovell, a market maker in Micron options at the Pacific Exchange, agreed the stock was catching up to the recent rally in the technology sector.
He said it appeared investors were selling other technology stocks and buying Micron.
In terms of the options, Kovell said one investor had been a big buyer of July calls in Micron and investors in general were buying a lot of at- and out-of-the-money calls.
"There's been a lot of speculative buying in at- and out-of-the-money (calls), and other than that there's a decent amount of volume but not a lot one way or the other," he said.
The Micron July 45 calls were most active, with turnover of 6,685 contracts. The July 47-1/2 calls traded more than 1,900 contracts and the July 50 calls traded more than 3,400.
The July 42-1/2 calls also were busy, with volume of nearly 4,200 contracts.
In the August series, the August 45 calls traded about 4,880 contracts.
Among Micron puts, the July 45 and August 45 were the only two that traded more than 1,000 contracts.
Traders said implied volatility in Micron options was up slightly but not extraordinarily.
"Volatilities are nothing out of whack," the trader in Chicago said. "I'm sure they're a little higher than average, but pretty much in line."
Kovell added that volatilities were up mainly in the front-month options, which expire at the end of the week.
In other activity, Intel Corp options were extremely active at the American Stock Exchange as the stock rose 1-1/2 to 78-3/8 on the first day of post-split trading.
The Intel July 77-1/2 call traded 10,720 contracts, making it the most active. The July 80 call traded 9,820 and the July 75 put traded 9,855.
Options analysts said a new phenomenon that has appeared recently is heavy call buying before and after a stock split.

Bernard Schaeffer, head of Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, called the phenomenon "stock split fever" and said it could "mark the beginning of a change in the 'fear-driven' environment that has been so healthy for the bull market of the 1990's."

He said in a report that "stock split fever" is not yet an indication of a market-topping environment but "has definitely been a 'shot across the bow' of this bull market, to which one must stay alert."
